text.p: As Dec 1 was a holiday marking Romania's national day, no local daily newspapers were printed on Monday, with the exception of Libertatea.
Here are highlights of stories in this paper. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Oltchim SA chemical plant won a bourse quotation, bringing to 17 the number of listed stocks.
- Romania is expected to face petrol shortages until the end of the year due to lack of hard currency to import crude.
- The prices of milk and dairy products are expected to rise by up to 20 percent.
- Ex-president Ion Iliescu, now leader of the Party of Social Democracy, pledged to restructure the party and give it new lines of action before year's end.

- Controversial Syrian businessman Zaher Iskandarani says in interview he is the largest single individual investor in Romania. Iskandarani was recently released from jail pending a trial for alleged cigarette smuggling and tax dodging worth 41 billion lei.
- Romanians gathered by tens of thousands in Alba Iulia on Sunday to hear President Emil Constantinescu speak in the Transylvanian town.
- Constantinescu left for Lisbon on Sunday to attend the OSCE summit.
- Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea is expected to announce the new cabinet on Thursday. ($=3,591 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 312 0264
